full_title: ATLAS: Adaptive Technology for Location and Spatial Support
all_authors: Maan Kumawat, HTI Lab Team, Siddharth Siddharth
publication_venue: HTI Lab Assistive Tech Showcase / Ongoing Project
research_domain: Assistive Wearable Technology, Computer Vision, Spatial Depth Sensing, Mobility for Visually Impaired
core_problem: Visually impaired individuals face severe navigation hazards from obstacles like stairs, drop-offs, and walls. Traditional solutions rely on expensive depth sensors, static maps, or cloud connectivity that introduces high latency.
system_summary: ATLAS is a wearable, real-time spatial fusion system acting as a digital guide dog. It combines dual Time-of-Flight (ToF) sensors and low-latency computer vision to deliver obstacle awareness and directional guidance entirely on-device.
sensing_and_hardware: Dual STMicroelectronics VL53L5CX multizone ToF sensors on dual I2C buses (90 deg FOV, 8x16 depth matrix), USB RGB camera (640x480 @ 30 FPS), Raspberry Pi 5 core, MAX98357A I2S amplifier with speaker for voice guidance, and GPIO PWM haptic buzzer for proximity warnings.
ai_models_and_algorithms: Lightweight YOLOv8 object detection on Raspberry Pi 5, 8x16 dual-sensor depth matrix stitching, Spatial Fusion Engine mapping 2D AI bounding boxes onto 3D depth grids for geometry-aware obstacle coordinates, and eSpeak-NG TTS for contextual voice alerts.
dataset_used: Custom obstacle dataset and COCO-pretrained YOLOv8 object classes (people, chairs, obstacles, vehicles).
key_results_and_metrics: Sweeping 90-degree field of view, sub-50ms local processing latency on Raspberry Pi 5 without cloud dependency, detects structural hazards (stairs, drop-offs) and provides precise proximity down to 12cm.
live_demonstration_aspects: Wearable rig demo with user wearing camera and dual-ToF sensors; system provides real-time natural voice guidance (e.g. Caution! Person very close, 12cm ahead) and dynamic haptic vibration as obstacles approach.
conversational_voice_pitch_1_sentence: ATLAS is an assistive wearable digital guide dog that fuses dual depth sensors with real-time AI vision on a Raspberry Pi to help visually impaired individuals navigate safely.
conversational_voice_pitch_detailed: ATLAS is our wearable assistive navigation system for the visually impaired. Running completely on a Raspberry Pi 5, it fuses dual Time-of-Flight depth sensors with a camera running YOLO object detection. It constructs a 3D semantic depth map in real time and gives audio and vibration alerts so users know precisely what obstacle is ahead and how many centimeters away it is.
keywords: wearable, assistive technology, visual impairment, Time of Flight, VL53L5CX, YOLOv8, Raspberry Pi 5, spatial fusion, haptic feedback, audio guidance, navigation

full_title: AdaptAI: A Personalized Solution to Sense Your Stress, Fix Your Mess, and Boost Productivity
lead_authors: Rushiraj Gadhvi*, Soham Petkar*, Priyansh Desai* (*Equal contribution)
all_authors: Rushiraj Gadhvi, Soham Petkar, Priyansh Desai, Shreyas Ramachandran, Siddharth Siddharth
lab_and_institution: HTI Lab, Plaksha University, Mohali, Punjab, India
research_domain: Affective Computing, Workplace Well-being, Physiological Sensing, Autonomous Task Agents
core_problem: Most productivity tools give the same generic suggestions to everyone. They fail to sense real-time physical or cognitive stress, ignore individual work routines, and frequently interrupt people during focused work.
system_summary: AdaptAI is a multimodal affective AI productivity system that senses real-time stress, tasks, and environment to automate routine administrative chores and deliver personalized well-being interventions without disrupting flow.
sensing_and_hardware: Egocentric vision camera, ambient audio microphone, heart rate monitor (photoplethysmography/ECG for HRV analysis), motion IMU sensors, and on-screen desktop activity logger.
ai_models_and_algorithms: 15-minute rolling window Processing Module creating structured state summaries; External Task Agents for automated email replies and calendar scheduling via voice/text; Personalized Intervention Pipeline; and Tone-adaptive Conversation Agent (TCA) modulating tone (motivating in high stress, neutral in low stress).
dataset_used: Empirical user study across 15 working professionals (ages 19-42) executing 4 realistic workplace tasks: Math Tests, Typing Speed, Web Coding, and Data Entry.
key_results_and_metrics: Statistically significant reductions in NASA-TLX: Data Entry showed cuts in Mental Demand (p=0.011), Physical Demand (p=0.005), Temporal Demand (p=0.031), and Effort (p=0.037). Coding showed significant drop in Frustration (p=0.021). Post-task ratings demonstrated higher user focus (3.98 vs 3.59, p=0.0399), higher task satisfaction (3.85 vs 3.28, p=0.0230), and lower stress levels (2.72 vs 3.16, p=0.0256).
live_demonstration_aspects: Demonstrates a user performing complex coding or data entry while stress increases; AdaptAI detects the stress spike from heart rate, automates routine calendar and email tasks in the background, and gently speaks in an empathetic, motivating tone to ease workload without breaking flow.
conversational_voice_pitch_1_sentence: AdaptAI is an affective workplace assistant that reads your physiological stress and task load to automate routine tasks and adapt its conversational tone to keep you in the zone.
conversational_voice_pitch_detailed: AdaptAI senses your real-time stress and workload using wearable cameras, heart rate monitors, and screen activity. When it detects high pressure during intense work, it automatically handles routine chores like calendar invites and emails, while adjusting its tone to be calm and motivating so you stay productive without burning out.
keywords: affective computing, stress sensing, heart rate variability, productivity, NASA-TLX, tone adaptation, automated agents, workplace well-being

full_title: Dhvani: A Weakly-supervised Phonemic Error Detection and Personalized Feedback System for Hindi
all_authors: Arnav Rustagi, Satvik Bajpai, Nimrat Kaur, Siddharth Siddharth
lab_and_institution: HTI Lab, Plaksha University, Mohali, India
research_domain: Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Training (CAPT), Speech Recognition, Phonetics, Indic Language Technologies
core_problem: While Computer-Assisted Pronunciation Training (CAPT) systems are common for English, a major gap exists for Indian languages like Hindi for second-language learners who struggle with subtle phonemic contrasts like aspirated and retroflex sounds.
system_summary: Dhvani is a weakly-supervised CAPT system specifically engineered for the Hindi language that detects fine-grained phonemic pronunciation errors and delivers actionable corrective feedback with articulatory tongue placement diagrams.
sensing_and_hardware: Standard audio microphone capturing speech audio converted into Mel-Spectrogram frames.
ai_models_and_algorithms: Encoder-Decoder architecture featuring an R-CNN Mel-Spectrogram Encoder and an Attentive Recurrent Neural Network (A-RNN) Phoneme Decoder with a 67-unit Hindi phoneme classification head. Error detection calculates Levenshtein edit distance between canonical phoneme sequences and predicted phonemes. Generates articulatory feedback via 2D tongue-palate anatomical diagrams.
dataset_used: Trained on the MUCS dataset (4,892 sentences from 78 L1 speakers), web-scraped YouTube speech from L2 speakers (121 sentences from 15 speakers), and 2,000 synthetic sentences with deliberate mispronunciations generated using Suno-AI Bark text-to-speech.
key_results_and_metrics: Human evaluation on a 5-point Likert scale demonstrated statistically significant pronunciation improvement in 10 out of 13 targeted phonemes, successfully training users on historically difficult Hindi retroflex and aspirated sounds.
live_demonstration_aspects: A user speaks a Hindi sentence into the microphone; Dhvani highlights exact mispronounced phonemes in Devanagari script, highlights the phoneme deviation, and displays an anatomical tongue diagram showing exactly where the tongue should touch the palate.
conversational_voice_pitch_1_sentence: Dhvani is an AI pronunciation coach for Hindi that detects subtle phonemic errors in your speech and shows visual tongue-placement diagrams to help you pronounce difficult sounds correctly.
conversational_voice_pitch_detailed: Dhvani is our Hindi pronunciation trainer published at INTERSPEECH 2025. It listens to non-native speakers, breaks speech down into 67 distinct Hindi phonemes using deep learning, detects mispronunciations, and displays an interactive tongue position diagram showing exactly how to position your mouth to fix the accent.
keywords: Dhvani, CAPT, Hindi pronunciation, phonemic error detection, INTERSPEECH 2025, R-CNN, A-RNN, Levenshtein distance, articulatory tongue diagram, Indic languages, speech AI

full_title: GuideAI: A Real-time Personalized Learning Solution with Adaptive Interventions
lead_authors: Ananya Shukla*, Chaitanya Modi*, Satvik Bajpai* (*Equal contribution)
all_authors: Ananya Shukla, Chaitanya Modi, Satvik Bajpai, Siddharth Siddharth
publication_venue: ACM IUI 2026 (31st ACM Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces, Limassol, Cyprus)
research_domain: Intelligent Tutoring Systems, Multimodal Bio-Sensing, Affective Computing, AI in Education
core_problem: Current LLM tutors are reactive and text-centric. They only update after a user types a response and completely miss real-time physiological and behavioral signals of confusion, cognitive overload, fatigue, or disengagement. In a formative study of 66 learners, 42% abandoned AI tutors that failed to adapt.
system_summary: GuideAI is a closed-loop personalized tutoring system that fuses physiological, behavioral, and cognitive biosignals to dynamically deliver multi-tiered pedagogical interventions (Micro, Meso, Macro) across text, audio, image, and video.
sensing_and_hardware: Pupil Core eye tracking glasses (60 fps capturing pupil fixations, saccades, and dilation), Max-Health-Band smartwatch (200 Hz recording heart-rate variability metrics SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50), MediaPipe computer vision for posture monitoring (neck, shoulder, spinal tilt), iPad digital note-taking snapshots scored by GPT-4o for conceptual understanding, all synchronized via Lab Streaming Layer (LSL).
ai_models_and_algorithms: Real-time multi-modal state classifier modeling six learner states (High Cognitive Load, Low Focus/Understanding, High Attention, Stress, Low Engagement, Fatigue). Trigger policy requires state persistence across 3 observation windows with >0.6 confidence. Adaptive interventions operate on 3 tiers: Micro (pacing & chunking), Meso (curiosity prompts, box breathing, posture resets), and Macro (first-principles scaffolding).
dataset_used: Formative study with N=66 learners; controlled within-subjects experimental evaluation with N=25 participants (13 M, 12 F, ages 18-42) across machine learning, statistics, and biology subjects.
key_results_and_metrics: Published at ACM IUI 2026. Resulted in +16.5 percentage points mean problem-solving gain (up to +30 pp in audio), +10.3 percentage points recall gain, a 0.49 standard deviation reduction in mental demand (NASA-TLX), and a 0.54 reduction in frustration (p < 0.05). Significant improvements in learner focus (5.60 vs 4.85) and perceived understanding (5.50 vs 4.75).
live_demonstration_aspects: A learner wears the eye tracker and heart-rate band while studying on a tablet; when the student gets stuck or overwhelmed (pupils dilate, fixations stall), GuideAI detects cognitive overload in real time, pauses the lecture, summarizes key ideas into bite-sized chunks, or initiates a brief box-breathing exercise.
conversational_voice_pitch_1_sentence: GuideAI is an intelligent tutor from ACM IUI 2026 that monitors pupil dilation, heart rate, and posture to detect when you are confused or tired, instantly adjusting the lesson difficulty in real time.
conversational_voice_pitch_detailed: GuideAI revolutionizes AI tutoring by looking beyond text. Using smart eye-tracking and heart-rate bands, it tracks your cognitive load, focus, and fatigue as you learn. When it senses you getting overwhelmed or frustrated, it pauses, breaks down tough concepts, or initiates box-breathing, boosting learning retention by up to 30 percent.
keywords: GuideAI, intelligent tutoring, eye tracking, Pupil Core, heart rate variability, cognitive load, ACM IUI 2026, closed-loop interventions, affective learning, multimodal biosensing

full_title: PosePilot: An Edge-AI Solution for Posture Correction in Physical Exercises
all_authors: Rushiraj Gadhvi, Priyansh Desai, Siddharth Siddharth
lab_and_institution: HTI Lab, Plaksha University, Mohali, Punjab, India
publication_venue: Edge AI / Computer Vision Showcase, HTI Lab
research_domain: Edge AI, Computer Vision, Digital Health, Physical Exercise Guidance, Kinematics
core_problem: Most automated posture correction systems rely on rigid, static, rule-based heuristics that fail to adapt to varied human body types. Incorrect execution of exercises like Yoga causes chronic joint injuries, while reliance on cloud vision compromises user privacy in home gym settings.
system_summary: PosePilot is an end-to-end, edge-computed AI system that automatically recognizes human physical exercise poses in real time and provides continuous joint-by-joint corrective feedback, running quantized deep neural networks locally on low-cost microcomputers.
sensing_and_hardware: Standard RGB web camera or Pi Camera module connected to a Raspberry Pi 4 (4 GB RAM, 64 GB SSD), rendering real-time guidance onto a lightweight graphical display.
ai_models_and_algorithms: MediaPipe extracts 33 3D skeletal keypoints converted into 680 inter-joint angular features. A Vanilla LSTM processes temporal angle sequences to classify Yoga poses among 6 asanas. A Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM) with Multi-Head Attention forecasts expert joint trajectories and computes error deviation vectors. Quantized using TensorFlow Lite to INT8.
dataset_used: Custom dataset of 336 multi-view video recordings across six classical Yoga asanas (Utkatasana/Chair, Virabhadrasana/Warrior, Adho Mukha Svanasana/Downward Dog, Bhujangasana/Cobra, Vrikshasana/Tree, Trikonasana/Triangle) performed by 14 practitioners (10 male, 4 female, ages 17-25) across 4 camera angles.
key_results_and_metrics: Ultra-fast edge execution on Raspberry Pi 4: Pose Recognition operates at 330.65 FPS (1.1 MB model) and Pose Correction operates at 6.42 FPS (41 MB model). INT8 quantization achieves significant speedup with only 1.0% loss in recognition accuracy and 1.3% in correction accuracy.
live_demonstration_aspects: A user stands in front of a camera and performs a yoga pose like Utkatasana (Chair Pose); the Raspberry Pi detects the pose instantly and overlays error warnings (e.g., Incorrect Elbow Position Detected) with directional arrows indicating how to align joints safely.
conversational_voice_pitch_1_sentence: PosePilot is an edge-AI yoga coach running on a Raspberry Pi that tracks your body joints in real time and gives instant visual feedback to correct your posture and prevent injuries.
conversational_voice_pitch_detailed: PosePilot uses lightweight AI models on a Raspberry Pi 4 to monitor your physical exercises. By tracking 33 skeletal body joints using MediaPipe and recurrent neural networks, it recognizes your yoga poses at over 300 frames per second, detects improper posture, and gives instant corrective guidance without sending video data to the cloud.
keywords: PosePilot, Edge AI, Raspberry Pi 4, posture correction, Yoga asanas, MediaPipe, LSTM, BiLSTM, Multi-Head Attention, TensorFlow Lite, INT8 quantization, computer vision

full_title: Saliency-guided Emotion Modeling: Predicting Viewer Reactions from Video Stimuli
lab_and_institution: HTI Lab, Plaksha University, Mohali, Punjab, India
publication_venue: Affective Computing & Multimedia Research, HTI Lab
research_domain: Affective Computing, Visual Saliency, Facial Action Units, Emotion AI, Multimedia Analytics
core_problem: Conventional affective computing relies almost exclusively on facial expressions and self-reported surveys to deduce emotional reactions to video content, completely ignoring visual saliency—the attention-grabbing visual regions within the video that trigger those emotional responses.
system_summary: This research pioneers the integration of visual saliency features with facial expression analysis to model viewer emotional valence and arousal, uncovering how focal attention regions directly influence affective reactions.
sensing_and_hardware: High-definition video cameras capturing viewer facial expressions synchronized with video stimuli playback.
ai_models_and_algorithms: HD2S deep saliency network to predict gaze-salient regions in video frames; OpenFace 2.0 toolkit extracting 18 facial Action Units (AUs); Canonical Correlation Analysis (CCA) and Pearson correlation linking saliency metrics (Saliency Area, Number of Salient Regions) to continuous Valence-Arousal scores and facial AUs.
dataset_used: Benchmarked on the MAHNOB-HCI multimodal database, comprising 527 video trials with synchronized facial videos, audio, and self-reported affective ratings.
key_results_and_metrics: Discovered that video frames with multiple salient regions evoke high valence (positive emotion) and low arousal (calmness), whereas a single dominant salient region induces low valence (negative emotion) and high arousal (urgency/anger). Uncovered a critical discrepancy between facial Action Units and self-reports (e.g., AU23 Chin Raiser correlated with anger even when self-reports differed), proving facial expressions alone are insufficient for emotion detection.
live_demonstration_aspects: Demonstration showing a video stimulus side-by-side with its real-time HD2S saliency heat map and the viewer OpenFace Action Unit detector, illustrating how viewer emotional state shifts dynamically as the video focal points change.
conversational_voice_pitch_1_sentence: This project studies how the attention-grabbing regions in videos shape our emotions, showing that where your eyes look directly influences whether you feel calm or agitated.
conversational_voice_pitch_detailed: Our saliency-guided emotion project uncovers the link between visual attention and emotional response. By pairing deep video saliency models with facial muscle tracking across 500 video trials, we found that scattered visual focal points induce calm, happy emotions, while a single intense focal point triggers high-stress, urgent reactions.
keywords: visual saliency, affective computing, emotion modeling, valence arousal, Action Units, OpenFace, HD2S, MAHNOB-HCI, Canonical Correlation Analysis, facial expression

full_title: The World of AI: A First-Year Course Bridging Technical Foundations and Societal Impact
all_authors: Siddharth Siddharth, Brainerd Prince, Amol Harsh, Shreyas Ramachandran
research_domain: AI Pedagogy, Engineering Education, AI Ethics, Societal Impact & Sustainability
core_problem: Traditional engineering curricula teach AI purely through mathematics and coding syntax, creating a dangerous blindspot regarding AI real-world societal harms, massive carbon/water footprints, algorithmic bias, and workforce automation.
system_summary: An innovative 14-week interdisciplinary first-year curriculum co-taught by engineering and humanities professors that pairs rigorous technical foundations with comprehensive ethical, environmental, and workplace impact analysis.
sensing_and_hardware: Interactive classroom pedagogical setup with dual-faculty instruction, LLM-based evaluation tools, and mixed-method rubric assessments.
ai_models_and_algorithms: 3 core instructional modules: Module 1 (Planet: energy consumption, water demands, sustainability), Module 2 (Society: algorithmic bias, fairness, inclusivity, data privacy), and Module 3 (Workplace: job displacement, automation, reskilling). LLM-based grading assistance with human spot-checks for open-ended reflections.
dataset_used: 168 first-year undergraduate engineering students (113 male, 55 female, ages 17-19) evaluated over a 14-week semester using validated instruments adapted from the Meta AI Literacy Scale (MAILS) and UNESCO AI Ethics Readiness framework.
key_results_and_metrics: Statistically significant gains across all 5 evaluation rubrics with large effect sizes (r = 0.47 to 0.77). Average student ratings on AI societal literacy increased to 6.5–7.5 out of 10. The highest learning gains were recorded in proposing ethical AI solutions and identifying responsibility and governance safeguards.
live_demonstration_aspects: Demonstration of the interactive AI ethics curriculum, highlighting student capstone presentations that analyze the carbon cost of training large models and showcase student-built algorithmic fairness safeguards.
conversational_voice_pitch_1_sentence: The World of AI is our flagship first-year curriculum bridging technical AI coding with hands-on education in AI ethics, sustainability, and societal impact.
conversational_voice_pitch_detailed: The World of AI is an innovative course at Plaksha that teaches first-year engineering students not just how to build AI models, but how AI affects energy consumption, societal bias, and future jobs. Co-taught by tech and humanities faculty, our research shows it creates massive gains in how students design responsible, ethical AI solutions.
keywords: AI education, AI ethics, engineering pedagogy, sustainability, algorithmic bias, UNESCO AI Ethics, MAILS, societal impact, curriculum design
